post.description:
Reads the file as bytes — UTF-8, or Windows-1252 when it is not valid UTF-8 — with a comma, semicolon or tab delimiter, and checks its header cell by cell against every template ever issued (ADR-0052). **Writes nothing.** Answers every data row against the roster and what is stored: a row is `refused` when it cannot be attributed to exactly one active member; a ready row carries twelve cells, each `new`, `changed`, `unchanged`, `not_provided` or `refused`, with the reason on the row. A blank cell is not provided and would change nothing (ADR-0051). `UPLOAD_TEMPLATE_MISMATCH` and `UPLOAD_MALFORMED_CSV` (422) refuse the whole file; `ASSET_TOO_LARGE` (413) above 1 MiB.

**Requires `data_upload:upload_and_preview`.** See `docs/00-product/roles-and-permissions.md`.

info.title: AgencyBoost API
info.description:
Multi-tenant SaaS for insurance agency offices (KPM).

Every failure uses one envelope — `{ error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }` — and every `code` has a row in `docs/02-specs/api/error-catalog.md`. **Branch on the code, never on the message.**

A resource in another tenant answers `404`, not `403`: a `403` would confirm the id exists.

ownerMembershipId.description: The membership whose lead it is, never a user id.

thisMonth.description: **Derived** (P7-T5): is there a commitment for the office’s current month? Nothing clears it, so it cannot be left true for an agent who has not opened the app since March.

committedMonths.description: Every month this lead was promised for, oldest first, in the office’s timezone. The archive behind *did they do what they said* — written when the promise is made rather than swept somewhere when the month ends.

version.description: What a later write pins, so two people cannot overwrite each other.

flags.description: Computed on read, never stored — a stored flag is one that is wrong at midnight. A closed lead carries none. **A commitment for this month does not suppress them**, unlike the prototype, which shows only the green chip on a lead that is also two weeks overdue.

lastEditedBy.description: Who last changed this lead, when that was not the agent whose lead it is (ADR-0044) — `null` otherwise. A proxy edit is recognisable by `updatedBy` differing from `ownerMembershipId`: two columns, so no flag is needed.

overdueDays.description: How late, in the office’s own calendar days — `null` unless `flags` carries `overdue`. Beside `flags` rather than inside it: `flags` is what the list filters on, and a filter key carrying a number is one nobody can match against.

total.description: Matching the filter, not on this page.

committedThisMonth.description: Open leads promised for the office’s **current** month — the glossary’s *Commitment*. Nothing clears it: a promise carries the month it was made for (P7-T5).

recruitmentPipelineNow.description: `RECRUITMENT_PIPELINE_NOW`: open recruitment candidates not on the stage that closes the pipeline. The office’s own `isTerminal` flag decides which that is (invariant §4).

recruitmentExpectedToClose.description: `RECRUITMENT_EXPECTED_TO_CLOSE`: open recruitment candidates on a stage the office flagged `isLateStage` (ADR-0043). A lead on the terminal stage is excluded by construction.

attention.description: How many open leads carry each attention flag. **They overlap** — a lead with no date and no remark is in two of them — so they do not sum to `open`. The keys are the values `GET /leads?attention=` takes, so a count links straight to the rows behind it.

type.description: Null until the agent picks a ladder.

contact.description: Refused without a lawful basis — LEAD_CONSENT_REQUIRED.

lawfulBasis.description: Why these details may be held (UU 27/2022).

thisMonth.description: The agent’s own commitment for the month.

type.description: Null until the agent picks a ladder.

contact.description: Refused without a lawful basis — LEAD_CONSENT_REQUIRED.

lawfulBasis.description: Why these details may be held (UU 27/2022).

thisMonth.description: The agent’s own commitment for the month.

version.description: The `version` this patch was written against. Refused with `409 VERSION_CONFLICT` if the lead has moved on — two people in one 1-on-1 on two devices is the realistic case.
The version this write was read at.

statusCode.description: Any **active** stage of this lead’s own ladder, at any time (ADR-0045). Refused for the other pipeline’s stages, for an archived one, and for a lead that is already closed.

version.description: The version this write was read at.

outcome.description: `won` needs the stage that closes the pipeline; `lost` needs nothing; `null` reopens. Reopening appends no transition — the lead has not moved.
